title: Console usage heatmap & sparsity-curated fact tables
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create materialized, curated fact tables that power Console UI heatmaps and tenant-level model usage exploration. The goal is a set of compact, pre-aggregated tables (heatmap_facts, tenant_model_popularity, latency_cost_buckets) that trade off raw cardinality for fast interactive queries while preserving accuracy for SLO/cost attribution. Focus areas: time bucketing, dynamic bucketning for sparsely-invoked tenants, storage-efficient encodings for model+route dimensionality, and robust incremental upsert workflow for streaming events.
acceptance_criteria: A heatmap_facts MV exists with tenancy, model_family, time_bucket, token_count_bucket, avg_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, total_tokens, invocation_count and is refreshable within 10 minutes of event arrival
Queries that power Console heatmap UI run under 600ms for 95% of queries on production dataset using the new curated tables
Materialized views handle tenant sparsity: for tenants < 100 invocations/day, records are stored in an aggregated sparse tier minimizing row count but still surfaced in UI
ETL job has idempotent upsert pattern and backfill for 90 days with monitored lag metric
tasks: Prototype sampling and bucketing algorithm on 30-day sample data
Implement CDC-upsert pipeline: streaming ingestion -> staging -> dedupe/compact -> write to curated tables
Create materialized view refresh strategy and partitioning scheme
Build CI SQL tests and performance benchmarks
Instrument Console queries to point at new tables and flag for gradual rollout
Add dashboards: freshness, row growth, query latency, top-k tenants with sparse tiering

design_decisions: Use multi-tier time bucketing: 1-minute for heavy tenants, 5-minute for medium, 1-hour for sparse tenants to balance query latency vs storage
Represent model identity with (model_family, model_fingerprint) to collapse minor variant churn in Console views
Store token_count as exponential buckets (1-8,9-32,33-128,129-512,>512) to avoid high cardinality and accelerate histograms
Two-tier storage: hot materialized tables (partitioned by date + tenant_hash) and sparse compact table that stores aggregate rows for very low-volume tenants
Adopt MERGE-based upserts with event_id dedupe and watermark gating rather than eventual consistency-only approach to avoid UI-visible double-counts
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: double-counts during backfill/stream overlap. Mitigation: watermark gating + window_id + idempotent MERGE + compaction window
Risk: query performance regressions when many tenants query wide time ranges. Mitigation: precompute multi-level rollups and ensure Console UI queries route to appropriate rollup based on time span
Risk: storage blowup from model churn. Mitigation: model_fingerprint bucketing and TTL on old variants combined with scheduled dedupe job
Risk: alert fatigue from false positive freshness alerts. Mitigation: tune freshness thresholds by tenant tier and include rolling median metrics
rollback_plan: If initial rollout causes console latency regressions, switch Console read path back to raw_event_views via feature-flag and pause MV refreshes. Re-run compaction and revert PR in platform repo. Notify customers if SLA is impacted.
qa_plan: Unit SQL tests for bucketing, integration tests for MERGE idempotency, load test with synthetic workload (10M events/day) to validate <600ms query P95, staging rollout with top 50 tenants for 48h
monitoring_playbook: Dashboards: MV refresh lag, streaming lag, row growth, P95 query latency. Alerts: MV_refresh_lag > 20m for hot tier, duplicate_count_rate > 0.1%
next_steps: Complete gating for backfill overlap (2d), finish UI integration and flag rollout (3d), execute staged rollout and monitor first-week metrics
notes: This ticket focuses on storage-efficient curated tables for interactive Console exploration. Billing-level cost attribution remains in a separate flow (ENG-43127) but will join via join keys defined in this schema. Ensure column naming parity with cost facts team.
